q-162231.name: Question 1
q-162231.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=x\,i-z\,j+y\,k$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [0,2).$
q-162231.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2,\,y=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =x\,i-z\,j+y\,k \\  & =2\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,k \\  & =0\,i-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k) \\  & =2\cdot 0+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)+\pi {cos}^{2}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\pi \,\text{d}t \\  & =\pi [t]_{0}^{2} \\  & =\pi (2-0) \\  & =2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the circulation Γ of the vector field F(x,y,z)=xi−zj+yk along the closed curve C given by r(t)=2i+cos⁡(πt)j+sin⁡(πt)k for t∈[0,2).

EXPLANATION

The circulation Γ measures the total work done by a force F in moving a particle along a closed curve C. It is given by the formula Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

Along the curve C, we have x=2,y=cos⁡(πt),z=sin⁡(πt).

So,

F(r(t))=xi−zj+yk=2i−sin⁡(πt)j+cos⁡(πt)k.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=ddt(2)i+ddt(cos⁡(πt))j+ddt(sin⁡(πt))k=0i−πsin⁡(πt)j+πcos⁡(πt)k.

Therefore,

F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(2i−sin⁡(πt)j+cos⁡(πt)k)⋅(−πsin⁡(πt)j+πcos⁡(πt)k)=2⋅0+(−sin⁡(πt))⋅(−πsin⁡(πt))+cos⁡(πt)⋅πcos⁡(πt)=πsin2⁡(πt)+πcos2⁡(πt)=π.

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫02F(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫02πdt=π[t]02=π(2−0)=2π

q-162229.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=-y\,i+x\,j$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+2\,k$ for $t\in [0,2).$
q-162229.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,z=2.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =-y\,i+x\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)\,k \\  & =-2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+0\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j)\cdot (-2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+0\,k) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\cdot (-2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+0\cdot 0 \\  & =2\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)+2\pi {cos}^{2}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2\pi \,\text{d}t \\  & =2\pi [t]_{0}^{2} \\  & =2\pi (2-0) \\  & =4\pi \end{aligned}
$$

q-162238.problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=(y-x)\,i$ along the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=({t}^{2}-t)\,i+({t}^{3}-t)\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [0,1).$
q-162238.worked_solution:
The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{2}-t,\,y={t}^{3}-t,\,z=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(y-x)\,i \\  & =({t}^{3}-t-{t}^{2}+t)\,i \\  & =({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,i.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)\,)\,k \\  & =(2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-1)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\,({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\,i\,)\cdot (\,(2t-1)\,i+(3{t}^{2}-1)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)\,k\,) \\  & =({t}^{3}-{t}^{2})\cdot (2t-1)+0\cdot (3{t}^{2}-1)+0\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t) \\  & =2{t}^{4}-{t}^{3}-2{t}^{3}+{t}^{2} \\  & =2{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(\,2{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+{t}^{2}\,)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{2{t}^{5}}{5}-\frac{3{t}^{4}}{4}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{2}{5}-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{3})-(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{60}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=({t}^{2}-t)\,i+(t-{t}^{3})\,j+(2{t}^{2}-2t)\,k$ for $t\in [0,1).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=y\,i+x\,k,$ evaluate the integral

$$
{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$
q-161928.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x={t}^{2}-t,\,y=t-{t}^{3},\,z=2{t}^{2}-2t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+x\,k \\  & =(t-{t}^{3})\,i+({t}^{2}-t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-{t}^{3})\,j-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{2}-2t)\,k \\  & =(2t-1)\,i+(1-3{t}^{2})\,j+(4t-2)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((t-{t}^{3})\,i+({t}^{2}-t)\,k)\cdot ((2t-1)\,i+(1-3{t}^{2})\,j+(4t-2)\,k) \\  & =(t-{t}^{3})\cdot (2t-1)+0\cdot (1-3{t}^{2})+({t}^{2}-t)\cdot (4t-2) \\  & =t-4{t}^{2}+5{t}^{3}-2{t}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∮}_{C}F\cdot dr \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(t-4{t}^{2}+5{t}^{3}-2{t}^{4})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={[\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}-\frac{4{t}^{3}}{3}+\frac{5{t}^{3}}{4}-\frac{2{t}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}-\frac{4}{3}+\frac{5}{4}-\frac{2}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{60}\end{aligned}
$$

Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [-1,1).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=y\,i+x\,k,$ evaluate the integral

$$
{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$
q-162324.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,z=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+x\,k \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,k \\  & =-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,k) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))+0\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)) \\  & =-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)-\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∮}_{C}F\cdot dr \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)-\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t))\,\text{d}t \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{1}(\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+\frac{\pi }{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)))\,\text{d}t \\  & =-{[\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)}{2}+\frac{\pi t}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)}{4}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =-[0+\frac{\pi }{2}+0-(0-\frac{\pi }{2}+0)] \\  & =-\pi \end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+3\,j+yz\,k \\  & =(2{t}^{2}+1)\,i+3\,j+(2{t}^{2}+1)({t}^{2}-1)\,k \\  & =(2{t}^{2}+1)\,i+3\,j+(2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2}-1)\,k.\end{aligned}

q-162892.name: Question 10
q-162892.problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,j+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,k$ for $t\in [-1,1).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=2y\,i-2x\,j+{e}^{z-2y}\,k,$ evaluate the integral

$$
{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$
q-162892.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t),\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,z=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t).
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =2y\,i-2x\,j+{e}^{z-2y}\,k \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+{e}^{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)}\,k \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+k.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))\,k \\  & =-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+k)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,i+\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,j+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,k) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\cdot (-\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t))-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\cdot \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+1\cdot 2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =-2\pi {sin}^{2}⁡(\pi t)-2\pi {cos}^{2}⁡(\pi t)+2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t) \\  & =-2\pi +2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∮}_{C}F\cdot dr \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(-2\pi +2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t))\,\text{d}t \\  & =[-2\pi t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)]_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(-2\pi (1)+0)-(-2\pi (-1)+0) \\  & =-4\pi \end{aligned}
$$

q-162371.name: Question 11
q-162371.problem:
Use Stokes' theorem to evaluate 

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,
$$

where $\text{curl}\,F=⟨y,\,2yz,\,-{z}^{2}+1⟩,$ and $C$ is the intersection of the half-cone $z=-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ and the plane $z=-3.$ The curve $C$ is oriented counter-clockwise when viewed from above.
q-162371.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

There are many surfaces whose boundary is the curve $C$ representing the intersection of the half-cone $z=-\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ and the plane $z=-3.$ One such surface would be the plane $S$ with the equation 

$$
z=g(x,y)=-3.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-3)=0 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into the expression for $\text{curl}\,F:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F\,{|}_{z=g(x,y)} & =⟨y,\,2yz,\,-{z}^{2}+1⟩{|}_{z=-3} \\  & =⟨{{y}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{-6y}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{-8}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y\cdot 0-(-6y)\cdot 0-8)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}-8\,\text{d}A,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is region enclosed by the projection of $C$ onto the $xy$-plane.

Notice that the projection of $C$ onto the $xy$-plane is the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9$ with radius $3$ centered at the origin. Therefore, using the change of variables to polar coordinates

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\text{d}A=r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta ,
$$

 

we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}-8\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}-8\cdot r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =-8{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}r\,\text{d}r \\  & =-8[\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi }\cdot {[\frac{{r}^{2}}{2}]}_{r=0}^{r=3} \\  & =-8(2\pi -0)\cdot (\frac{9}{2}-0) \\  & =-72\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2})=2(x-1) \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x-1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2})=2(y+1)\end{aligned}

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\text{d}A=r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta ,

q-162363.worked_solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

There are many surfaces whose boundary is the curve $C$ representing the intersection of the paraboloid $z={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}$ and the boundary of our infinite vertical column. One such surface is our paraboloid $S$ with the equation 

$$
z=g(x,y)={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=2x \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})=-2y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into expression for $\text{curl}\,F:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{curl}\,F\,{|}_{z=g(x,y)} & =⟨y,\,x,\,2⟩{|}_{z={x}^{2}-{y}^{2}} \\  & =⟨y,\,x,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨{{y}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{x}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{2}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y\cdot (2x)-x\cdot (-2y)+2)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2\,\text{d}A,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is region enclosed by the projection of $C$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{2}\,2\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

Let C be the intersection of the hyperbolic paraboloid z=x2−y2 and the boundary of the infinite vertical column enclosed by the planes x=±1, y=±2. Given that the curve C is oriented counter-clockwise when viewed from above and curlF=⟨y,x,2⟩, the circulation of F along C can be written as ∮CF⋅dr=

a
∫−11∫−222xydydx
b
∫−11∫−2xx2−y2dydx
c
∫−11∫−222+2xydydx
d
∫−11∫−222dydx
e
∫−11∫−2x4+2xydydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let S be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary C with positive orientation. If a vector field F has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains S, then Stokes' theorem states that

∮CF⋅dr=∬ScurlF⋅dS.

There are many surfaces whose boundary is the curve C representing the intersection of the paraboloid z=x2−y2 and the boundary of our infinite vertical column. One such surface is our paraboloid S with the equation

z=g(x,y)=x2−y2.

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph z=g(x,y):

∂g∂x=∂∂x(x2−y2)=2x∂g∂y=∂∂y(x2−y2)=−2y

Next, we substitute the equation z=g(x,y) into expression for curlF:

curlF|z=g(x,y)=⟨y,x,2⟩|z=x2−y2=⟨y,x,2⟩=⟨y⏟P,x⏟Q,2⏟R⟩

So, we have

∬ScurlF⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA=∬D(−y⋅(2x)−x⋅(−2y)+2)dA=∬D2dA,

where D is region enclosed by the projection of C onto the xy-plane, shown below.

Therefore, we obtain

∬D2dA=∫−11∫−222dydx.
